- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is falling, model underestimates downward momentum; add 2–5% downward bias to forecast.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; for 30-day forecasts, apply 1–2% mean reversion to historical 18-day average if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days or use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >10% for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–10% and re-evaluate sentiment correlation.
